input.quote: 14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.
input.rationale: The IP package meets the preferred position in full. § 14.1 confirms Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and pre-existing/independently developed IP, with no transfer to Vendor beyond a limited processing right to deliver the Services. § 14.2 vests ownership of each Deliverable in Customer on creation with an express present assignment (subject only to payment) plus personnel assignments and further-assurance cooperation. § 14.3 lets Vendor retain only Vendor Technology and routes any Vendor Technology embedded in or required to use a Deliverable through the perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence in § 13.2, which also permits modification, derivative works and contractor use. § 14.4 bars joint ownership absent a separate signed instrument and keeps feedback voluntary with Customer retaining unrestricted rights, and § 15.1 blocks model training on Customer Data without consent. No assignment of Customer IP or data to Vendor and no walk-away features. Minor, customary points noted only: the Customer Data definition (§ 1.3) carves out anonymized operational telemetry not linkable to Customer, and the Deliverable definition (§ 1.4) carves out unaided-memory know-how — neither is a material deviation, so no redline.
